title: What happens when you charge and when you drive
narration: When you plug in, the charger applies an electrical push. It drives lithium ions, charged bits of lithium, out of the positive side and into the graphite, where they slip between its thin layers like cards into a deck. Now the cell is charged, like water pumped up into a hilltop tank. When you drive, the water flows back down. The ions drift back to the positive side, while electrons take an outside route through the car's circuits, powering the car. Nothing is broken down, so this can repeat over and over.

visual_content.image_description: Simple diagram of a battery cell: lithium ions moving between graphite layers and the positive side, electrons looping through an outside wire
visual_content.caption: Plug in: ions move in. Drive: they flow back.
